title: Can 3M Continue Its Strong Capital Returns to Shareholders?
author: Na
description: 3M Company returned $3.8 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks in the first half of 2026, with $1.8 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization. The company expects adjusted operating cash flow of $5.8-$6.0 billion and free cash flow conversion above 100% for 2026, while raising its quarterly dividend by 6.8% in February 2026. Despite trading above industry valuation averages, 3M shares gained 3.6% over the past year compared to a 27.8% industry decline.

Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) reflects moderate confidence.

title: GE Aerospace Is Making a $12 Billion Acquisition. Here's What Investors Should Know.
author: Catie Hogan
description: GE Aerospace announced an $11.75 billion acquisition of Consolidated Precision Products (CPP), its largest deal since becoming independent in 2024. The acquisition addresses critical supply chain constraints by bringing a key aerospace castings supplier in-house, as CPP supplies approximately 25% of GE's needs. Financed with $7 billion cash and new debt, the deal is expected to boost adjusted profit per share and free cash flow in the first year, though it faces antitrust scrutiny. GE's $210 billion backlog extending into the 2030s necessitates the additional capacity.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The acquisition strategically addresses a critical supply chain bottleneck, secures manufacturing capacity to meet a $210 billion backlog, and is expected to boost profitability and free cash flow in the first year. Despite near-term balance sheet pressure and antitrust concerns, the long-term operational benefits and revenue visibility support a positive outlook.

title: Can RTX's GTF Aftermarket Expansion Boost Its Growth Outlook?
author: Na
description: RTX Corporation is expanding its commercial aerospace aftermarket opportunity through Pratt & Whitney's growing Geared Turbofan (GTF) engine support network, which now spans 21 facilities worldwide. The GTF family powers over 2,600 aircraft across multiple platforms, creating recurring maintenance and repair opportunities. In 2025, the GTF Advantage engine received certification for the Airbus A320neo family, designed to offer higher thrust and improved fuel efficiency. Pratt & Whitney's sales grew to $32.9 billion in 2025, with operating profit reaching $2.6 billion.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: RTX is expanding its aftermarket revenue opportunities through a growing GTF support network (21 facilities), 26% year-over-year increase in shop-visit output, new engine certification, and strong financial performance with Pratt & Whitney sales up 17% and operating profit up 30% in 2025. The company holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating.

title: GE Aerospace (GE) Registers a Bigger Fall Than the Market: Important Facts to Note

description: GE Aerospace fell 2.83% on September 9, 2026, underperforming the S&P 500's 0.48% decline. title: GE Expands Mission-Critical Castings Capacity Through CPP Acquisition
author: Zacks.Com
description: GE Aerospace announced an $11.75 billion acquisition of Consolidated Precision Products (CPP) from Warburg Pincus and Berkshire Partners. CPP manufactures precision castings and sub-assemblies for commercial and military aircraft engines. The deal aims to expand GE's casting capacity, strengthen its supply chain, and support growth in commercial engines, aftermarket, and defense markets. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2027.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: The acquisition strengthens GE's strategic position by expanding casting capacity and supply chain capabilities. The company benefits from robust demand for commercial engines, defense spending, and positive airline dynamics. However, this is tempered by concerns about high costs and restructuring expenses affecting margins.
